chunks: And it has been narrated from Abū Bakr ibn Abī Sammāl, who said:
I prayed Fajr behind Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, and when he finished his recitation in the second rakʿah, he raised his voice somewhat in the manner of recitation and said:
“O Allāh, forgive us, have mercy on us, grant us well-being, and pardon us in this world and the Hereafter.
Surely You have power over all things.”

key_terms.اللَّهُمَّ: O Allah; opening formula of supplication

ai.seo_question: What supplication did Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام recite in Fajr prayer after the recitation?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a supplication recited by Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام in the Fajr prayer after the recitation in the second rakʿah. It combines seeking forgiveness, mercy, well-being, and pardon in both this world and the Hereafter, and concludes with an affirmation of Allah’s absolute power.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1189 - Abu Bakr ibn Abi Samal who said:
"I prayed behind Abu Abdullah (as) for Fajr (dawn prayer). When he finished the recitation in the second rak'ah, he raised his voice slightly as if reciting and said:

Allahumma ighfir lana wa irhamna wa ‘afina wa ‘u‘fu ‘anna fi ad-dunya wa al-akhirah. Innaka ‘ala kulli shay’in qadeer
'O’ Allah (swt), forgive us, have mercy on us, grant us well-being, and pardon us in this world and the Hereafter.
Truly, You have power over all things.'".
